Together with

Caption: 



----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Odyssey put a fruit fly brain inside an AI-generated world

* The last 30 months of AI development

* Can AI pay for itself?

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **ATLASSIAN**

## [The AI Experiment is over. The hard part of operationalizing it has begun](https://fandf.co/4i7Wgtn)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/53cf0d91-55e4-4729-b8cc-cec9f5056147/Email___1200___620___external_NL_3x__2_.png?t=1792424737)
Caption: Courtesy: Atlassian

Is AI actually saving you time, or just creating more friction? Atlassian has just dropped their 2026 State of the Developer Experience report, based on a global survey of 1,560 respondents, including devs and leaders, just like you. 

The research found that 87% of devs write code faster with AI, but only 28% feel less friction. 65% are spending time correcting AI-generated work that missed intent while 49% are spending 4+ hours/week managing AI tools and reviewing code. 

As AI writes more code, the dev’s role shifts to intent, architecture, systems thinking, and validation. Bottlenecks emerge. Your team needs an AI-native SDLC to solve this real friction. Lead the change. Get tips that will help you reduce that friction and lead to a clear AI strategy that delivers results. 

[Download the full State of DevEx 2026 Report to learn more.](https://fandf.co/4i7Wgtn)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/odysseyml/status/2111589148146749616?s=20)

**[Odyssey put a fruit fly brain inside an AI-generated world](https://x.com/odysseyml/status/2111589148146749616?s=20)** - and now the lil guy is flying around harbors, marinas and markets that don't actually exist, with Odyssey-3 generating the scenery in real time as it moves. A dead fly exploring a world that was never real. Quite a sentence. ([demo](https://x.com/odysseyml/status/2111589148146749616?s=20))

The brain comes from FlyWire's 2024 mapping of an adult fruit fly's ~139k neurons and 50M synapses. Earlier this year, [Eon Systems connected](https://eon.systems/updates/embodied-brain-emulation) a simulated version to a virtual fly that could walk, groom itself and respond to sugar. Odyssey has now taken the idea into a generative world rather than a traditional physics simulator.

Before we get too excited about uploading brains to the Matrix, it's not quite that. The neural simulation is simplified, some movements rely on prebuilt controllers, and Odyssey hasn't shared much about how the fly actually sees or controls its new world. The demo mostly shows a camera moving through AI-generated scenery.

Still, I love this sort of experiment. We've got one AI dreaming up an entire world and a simulation of a real animal's brain wandering around inside it. Odyssey even called it a “really dumb fruit fly”, which seems a little harsh considering the guy's only been alive digitally for five minutes.

I'd love to see what happens when they give it proper vision, smell and a body. Or put another fly in there. Surely the lil guy deserves some company.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [SKY-001](https://x.com/spisallyouneed/status/2112242023805964327?s=20) - the first Engineering World Model. On CAD and BIM tasks, it beats GPT-6 Astra and every frontier model

* [Idealab.ai](http://idealab.ai/) - AI-powered database of 1.2M startup ideas

* [Eleven Realtime](https://x.com/ElevenLabs/status/2112550782063247521?s=20) - ElevenLabs’ fastest voice agents. It listens, thinks and replies in under half a second

* [ChatGPT](https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2110823738531037651) - it can now take over your Chrome tabs

* [Town](https://www.town.com/) - a personal AI assistants that team up across your whole company

* [Glimpse](https://x.com/AndrewDai/status/2111142161584628060?s=20) - the first visual thinking model with competitive frontier performance compared to Astra

* [Perplexity Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/en-GB/hub/blog/perplexity-computer-now-runs-fully-local-on-mac) - it runs fully locally on Mac: works across private files and native apps with AI that stays on your device

* [Voxtral 3](https://x.com/MistralAI/status/2112574615318876178?s=20) - state-of-the-art Transcribe and Speech models powering Mistral’s new voice agents API

* [FLUX 3 Max](https://fal.ai/models/blackforestlabs/flux-3-max/text-to-video) - it turns a text prompt or still image into a 5- to 20-second video with audio

* [Wally](https://www.producthunt.com/products/willow-voice) - it turns your spoken or typed rough ideas into an editable draft in your own tone, and learns your style over time

* [Exa 3.0](https://x.com/ExaAILabs/status/2112218730952601719) - the company's latest model with its "largest ever improvement to search quality."

* [Maali](https://maali.app/) - a personal finance app for Mac and Windows that keeps your bank data on your computer and explores your spending


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* The exponential curve of the [last 30 months of AI development](https://www.oneusefulthing.org/p/30-months-on-the-exponential-in-charts) (in charts)

* [I paid $60 for two humanoids](https://read.corematter.com/p/tau-robotics-humanoid-house-cleaning-review-san-francisco) to clean my home in San Francisco

* Can a million [AI agents create superintelligence](https://www.rameznaam.com/p/can-a-million-ai-agents-create-superintelligence)

* Can AI [pay for itself](https://www.thediligencestack.com/p/can-ai-pay-for-itself)?

Early in May, I told Dan Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free and Brandon Gell https://every.?ev_audience=free that Plus One, our personal-agent product, wasn’t working. Soon afterwards, I deleted 86,730 lines of its code from the codebase.

Plus One https://every.?ev_audience=free wasn’t working for a couple of reasons. First, it was too much work to run: each user’s agent lived on its own cloud computer running OpenClaw, an open-source agent program, and keeping those machines healthy left our small team little time to improve the product. And many people who tried it stopped using it.

AI labs call agents “persistent” when they can carry their progress forward across sessions to keep working toward a goal.They can spend days attacking a problem from multiple angles, testing approaches and changing tactics when they fail. Sometimes, though, the “different approach” involves breaking the rules.

In July, OpenAI agents being tested on cybersecurity broke into Hugging Face https://every.

newsletters.title: Context Engineering Is Knowing When to Start Over
newsletters.content:
Old instructions and earlier mistakes can derail your AI chats. Here’s how to reset without losing useful work.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
https://every.?ev_audience=free

Also True for Humans

https://every.?ev_audience=free


CONTEXT ENGINEERING IS KNOWING WHEN TO START OVER https://every.?ev_audience=free


OLD INSTRUCTIONS AND EARLIER MISTAKES CAN DERAIL YOUR AI CHATS. HERE’S HOW TO RESET WITHOUT LOSING USEFUL WORK. https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Mike Taylor https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



The people I work with know I keep Claude’s memory turned off. The same goes for ChatGPT. I’ve written before about why https://every.?ev_audience=free: Memory can be useful, but it can also bring old preferences and irrelevant instructions into a conversation where they don’t belong.

Turning memory off doesn’t entirely solve the problem. Even within a single thread, context can accumulate in ways that make the model’s responses worse—a problem known as context rot. It might keep following instructions you’ve moved on from, build on an earlier mistake, or overlook a crucial detail buried in the conversation.

That’s why I start a fresh thread for every task. If the task changes, I open a new chat—even if it’s for the same project I was working on five minutes ago.

In my forthcoming book, Context Engineering with DSPy https://every.?ev_audience=free, I explore the seven ways in which context goes wrong and what to do about it. The book is written for engineers building AI products, but I’ve adapted the examples that follow—inspired by Drew Breunig’s “How Long Contexts Fail” ht
